achieving overfilling or bottom-up deposition
Leveling agents are crucial for achieving overfilling or bottom-up deposition.

Presently, leveling agents on the market are predominantly organic dye-based leveling agents with quaternary ammonium cations and a halide ion, such as Janus green B (JGB), Diazine black (DB), Methylene blue (MB), and Alcian blue (ABPV).
Although these leveling agents can achieve remarkable filling efects under specific conditions, they are not resistant to high temperatures and are prone to decomposition.

Furthermore, these leveling agents are predominantly synthetic organic compounds or mixtures of various organic substances, resulting in high costs, notable toxicity, and pollution, along with certain quality and environmental concerns.
Therefore, it is necessary to search for leveling agents that are inexpensive, less toxic, stable, and exhibit good electroplating efects.
Most commonly used nondye leveling agents are nitrogen-containing heterocyclic or nonheterocyclic aromatic compounds.

evidence.quote: 底部 Co 镀层的沉积速率要高于外表面
文献中认为当达到还原电位时，吸附在阴极表面的 PEI 被破坏或掺杂进沉积层，从而导致局部溶液的电阻降低。根据这一现象，在进行 TSVs 填充时，盲孔底部的 PEI 浓度受传质影响而低于外部溶液的浓度，从而在底部形成 Co ^2 + 沉积的活化区域，而侧壁和外表面仍处在失活区域，从而导致底部 Co 镀层的沉积速率要高于外表面，如图 1-13c 所示。

evidence.quote: favorable frontier orbital energy gaps (ΔE)

Based on the ML model, we can perform high-throughput ΔE predictions across a large molecular space for preliminary assessment. To rapidly advance these predictions to experimental validation, we employed a commercially available (CA) dataset with unknown ΔE as the prediction set. Every molecule in the dataset is quality-controlled, eliminating delays and costs associated with synthetic feasibility. Spe cifically, we mapped the chemical space of the training set onto the Sigma–Aldrich catalog and retrieved 4355 nitrogen-containing organic compounds. After prioritizing candidates based on the predicted ΔE values, the top 1% were flagged as promising additives. Considering accessibility, toxicity, and cost, we selected three molecules — 2-amino pyrazine (APZ), 1-methylimidazole-4,5-dicarbonitrile (MIDCN), and 2- amino-4-ethylpyridine (AEP) — for subsequent experimental verification (Table S4). These candidates exhibited favorable frontier orbital energy gaps (ΔE), underscoring their adsorption activity on the metal surface.
